definitions.explanation: A popular Japanese dish of stir-fried wheat noodles with vegetables, meat, and a savory sauce. A staple of street food stalls at festivals and a common home-cooked meal.

examples.japanese: {昼|ひる}ごはんに{焼|や}きそばを{作|つく}った。
{屋台|やたい}の{焼|や}きそばはソースの{香|かお}りがたまらない。
examples.english: The aroma of sauce from the street stall yakisoba is irresistible.

examples.japanese: お{祭|まつ}りに{行|い}ったら、まず{焼|や}きそばとかき{氷|ごおり}を{買|か}うのが{定番|ていばん}だ。
examples.english: When you go to a festival, buying yakisoba and shaved ice first is the standard routine.

notes:
USAGE:
Despite the name containing そば (buckwheat noodles), {焼|や}きそば is made with {中華|ちゅうか}{麺|めん} (Chinese-style wheat noodles), not buckwheat noodles. The noodles are stir-fried on a griddle with cabbage, pork, and other ingredients, then seasoned with a thick Worcestershire-type sauce.

FORMS:
- ソース{焼|や}きそば: the standard sauce-flavored version
- {塩|しお}{焼|や}きそば: salt-flavored yakisoba
- {焼|や}きそばパン: a bread roll filled with yakisoba, popular at convenience stores and school cafeterias

CULTURAL NOTE:
{焼|や}きそば is closely associated with {祭|まつ}り (festivals) and {屋台|やたい} (food stalls). It is one of the most iconic {屋台|やたい} foods alongside たこ{焼|や}き.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {焼|や}きそばを{作|つく}る: to make yakisoba
- {焼|や}きそばを{焼|や}く: to cook yakisoba
- {屋台|やたい}の{焼|や}きそば: festival stall yakisoba
